answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to hold the umber of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random data indices; failure to return data matching the thread of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. Each copper-based bus connection must remain unique. Honest agents pay 120 watts to maintain their status, while fakes pay 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible.
